Philadelphia House Delegation issues statement on shooting of police officers
Rep. Morgan B. Cephas
October 10, 2026 | 11:07 AM
(Updated to reflect the tragic news about Officer Seiber)
"We are deeply saddened to learn of the passing of one of the officers shot in last night's attack. Please join us in keeping Officer Seiber's loved ones in your prayers."
PHILADELPHIA, Oct. 10 –
The Philadelphia House Delegation issued a statement on Saturday morning’s shooting of two Philadelphia Police Department officers responding to an emergency call.
“The shooting of these two officers responding to a 911 call about a man brandishing a gun on the porch of a West Philadelphia home is another senseless, horrific case of gun violence shattering the lives of people in our community.
“Our thoughts and prayers are with the officers – both of them parents – their loved ones and their brothers and sisters in uniform as they continue the never-ending job of rushing toward danger. We thank the emergency responders and the doctors and nurses of Penn Presbyterian for their heroic efforts in treating these two officers.
“This shooter allegedly waited for the officers to respond to the call and then ambushed them, then continued to fire on the officers who responded to save the fallen. We are grateful he was taken into custody and will now face justice.
“There are far too many incidents like this one – beyond standing with the community, we renew our pledge to advance legislation to stop gun violence and protect every person we serve.”
The
Philadelphia House Delegation
is chaired by
state Rep. Morgan Cephas
, D-Phila., and consists of 25 members of the Pennsylvania House of Representatives who represent Pennsylvania’s only county of the first class.

Cephas menopause bills pass the PA House
Rep. Morgan B. Cephas
October 7, 2026
HARRISBURG, Oct. 7 –
Two menopause bills sponsored by state Rep. Morgan Cephas, D-Phila., passed the state House today. This legislation would expand access to hormonal and non-hormonal therapy and ensure protection for employees experiencing pregnancy-related and menopause-related conditions in the workplace.
House Bill 1345 would provide Medicaid coverage for menopause treatments. This would help ensure all menopausal women can access the FDA-approved treatments for their symptoms and are made aware of the available options.
House Bill 2135 -- the Menopause and Perimenopause Workplace Protections and Accommodations Act -- would require employers to provide reasonable accommodation for these conditions. The bill also includes protection against denying employment because someone needs accommodation. House Bill 2135 passed with an amendment establishing that an employer may require reasonable documentation from a licensed healthcare provider to confirm the condition and the limitations or symptoms that require accommodation.
Both bills are part of the “No Time for a Pause” package of menopause legislation.
“I am thrilled that my colleagues voted to pass this important legislation to make sure treatments are accessible and affordable, and that women do not have to choose between their health and earning a living,” said Cephas. “Menopause and perimenopause affect millions of women in Pennsylvania. Every one of them deserves access to therapies that work for their symptoms.
“Women also make up half the workforce in our commonwealth. Many are between 40 and 64, the ages where women typically experience perimenopause and menopause. Those conditions should never cost a woman a job, a promotion or her dignity at work.
“While I am thrilled this legislation passed the House, I was disturbed to hear certain remarks from my colleagues about these conditions, including one who admitted he would not hire a woman due to menopause. These comments underscored the need for this legislation. We must continue to break the stigma, expand education about menopause and ensure protections for all Pennsylvania workers.”
Both bills now move to the state Senate for consideration.

Highmark Mann awarded $250K state grant
Funds will support educational and cultural programming
Rep. Morgan B. Cephas
October 1, 2026 | 2:15 PM
HARRISBURG, Oct. 1 –
Highmark Mann Center has been awarded a $250,000 state grant for operational support for its educational and cultural programming.
The announcement was made today by state Reps. Jennifer O’Mara, D-Delaware, chair of the House Democratic Caucus Southeast Delegation; Morgan Cephas, D-Phila., chair of the Philadelphia Delegation; and Roni Green, D-Phila., whose legislative district includes Highmark Mann.
A publicly owned facility operated by a nonprofit, Highmark Mann offers widely diverse programming and attracts more than 400,000 visitors annually. Its attendance has more than doubled since 2015.
The grant was awarded from a program at the state Department of Community and Economic Development.
“The Southeast Delegation advocated for this grant, because Highmark Mann is a treasured institution in our region,” O’Mara said. “It is much more than a performing arts center -- it has also grown to be a leader in educational offerings in the arts. We are proud to have Highmark Mann in our region and we’re proud to help support it.”
Working with Philadelphia public schools, Highmark Mann provides educational offerings to many underserved children, providing programming to nearly 5,000 students each year.
“Nestled in beautiful East Fairmount Park in West Philadelphia, the Highmark Mann Center is a beacon of togetherness for our communities,” Green said. “While it serves as a venue for nationally known artists and entertainment, it’s also been the backdrop for community events, learning, and growth for generations. I’m glad we’re able to support the programming and development at the Mann through this grant from DCED.”
“For 50 years, the Highmark Mann Center has been a recognizable focal point of the arts, entertainment, and education in Philadelphia and our southeastern counties,” Cephas said. “Our delegation is always happy to support funding for the Mann to amplify their informative and cultural opportunities for all people and every community.”

Philadelphia House Delegation condemns reported hate speech by GOP Rep.
Rep. Morgan B. Cephas
October 1, 2026 | 1:18 PM
HARRISBURG, Oct. 1
– The Philadelphia House Delegation issued a statement in support of Rep. Malcolm Kenyatta, D-Phila., and calling for the immediate resignation of Rep. Aaron Bernstine, R-Butler/Lawrence, following his reported hateful outburst directed at Kenyatta, according to recent reporting by
PennLive
:
“The Philadelphia House Delegation stands in support of our colleague from North Philadelphia Rep. Malcolm Kenyatta and echoes the call of the
PA Legislative Black Caucus
and
PA LGBTQ+ Equality Caucus
for the immediate resignation of Rep. Aaron Bernstine following his alleged disgusting, hate-filled tirade.
“There is no stronger advocate than Rep. Kenyatta for the promise of Pennsylvania and equality of all people. There is no place in the institution of the House of Representatives nor in this commonwealth for hate speech and the reported abhorrent rhetoric espoused by Rep. Bernstine. As elected officials, we must hold ourselves to a higher standard of conduct, a level which Rep. Bernstine has
repeatedly failed
.
“While we know that Rep. Kenyatta will continue to shine above the lowbrow spectacle of Rep. Bernstine and his ilk, we believe it’s time for the House Republican leaders and members to be accountable for their colleague, follow the lead of the majority of Pennsylvanians who reject those hateful views by publicly condemning Bernstine’s bluster, and demand that he do the right thing for Pennsylvania and the good people of Butler and Lawrence counties by resigning immediately.”
The
Philadelphia House Delegation
is chaired by
state Rep. Morgan Cephas
, D-Phila., and consists of 25 members of the PA House of Representatives who represent Pennsylvania’s only county of the first class.

Menopause awareness takes on a new meaning in PA
Rep. Morgan B. Cephas
September 29, 2026 | 4:17 PM
HARRISBURG, Sep. 29 –
State Sen. Maria Collett, and Reps. Melissa Shusterman, Liz Hanbidge and Morgan Cephas are celebrating the success of the
‘No Time for a Pause’
package of menopause-related legislation.
The No Time for a Pause package highlights legislative efforts for greater insurance coverage, workplace accommodations, preventative care and education on menopause. The state House reported seven of the bills out of committee and passed one bill in the chamber on a variety of topics covering:
Menopause Education
Insurance Coverage for Menopause
Pelvic Floor Health Insurance
Preventative Measures for Hip Fractures
Insurance Coverage for Vaginal Estrogen and to Prevent UTIs
Workplace Protections
Medicaid Coverage for Menopause
The makers of these bills, public health professionals, advocacy organizations and supporters celebrated these wins and the No Time for a Pause movement with
a rally and a further call to action
.
Shusterman explained, “Menopause is more than a minor inconvenience; it is a health crisis. From years of lost sleep and debilitating brain fog to frozen joints and brittle bones, these severe symptoms demand action. Every single piece of legislation in the
No Time for a Pause
package serves a purpose in delivering better care, education and treatment for the women of PA.
“My bills, House Bill 1827 and 2545, focus on preventative measures for hip fractures, UTIs and insurance coverage for vaginal estrogen. I’m also proud to announce my resolution, House Resolution 287, to direct the Joint State Government Commission to study workplace policies on perimenopause and menopause was approved by the House on a vote of 159-44. There is a LOT to celebrate today!”
“As a nurse and member of the Governor’s Advisory Commission on Women, I want to make sure that all women in Pennsylvania are equipped and empowered to handle the changes that come with menopause,” said Collett, D-Montgomery. “I'm proud to be working with champions like Representatives Liz Hanbidge, Leanne Krueger and Morgan Cephas to improve menopause education for healthcare providers, require insurance coverage for menopause care, and give patients the resources they need to lead healthy and fulfilling lives.”
“Menopause and perimenopause affect our health, our families, our work and our quality of life, yet too many people still feel unseen and unsupported,” said Cephas, D-Phila. “House Bills 1345 and 2135 are designed to expand access to treatment and prioritize the needs of aging populations in our workforce and healthcare system. Advancing this legislation helps us to break the stigma, raise awareness and ensure health equity.”
“For too long, women experiencing perimenopause and menopause have been overlooked in our health care system, workplaces and communities,” said Hanbidge, D-Montgomery. “The passage of this package is an important step toward changing that. Women deserve accurate information, evidence-based care and the support they need to stay healthy, work and thrive. Menopause affects women’s health, quality of life, careers and families, with an economic impact of $26.6 billion each year. This legislation recognizes that women’s health matters at every stage of life and begins breaking down the barriers that have held too many women back.”
Shusterman said women’s health has been ignored by government for far too long and it is past time menopause is not only talked about but also voted on. The No Time for a Pause campaign will continue to bring the topic of menopause to the forefront of conversations on women’s health in Pennsylvania.

Legislation would provide Medicaid coverage for menopause treatments and protect menopausal workers
Rep. Morgan B. Cephas
September 29, 2026 | 4:10 PM
HARRISBURG, Sept. 29 –
State Rep. Morgan Cephas, D-Phila., announced two menopause bills have advanced from committee. Both bills are part of the ‘No Time for a Pause’ package of menopause-related legislation.
House Bill 1345, which was reported out of the House Human Services Committee on Monday, would provide Medicaid coverage for hormonal and non-hormonal therapy to treat menopausal symptoms.
House Bill 2135, the Menopause and Perimenopause Workplace Protections and Accommodations Act, advanced from the House Labor and Industry Committee today. This legislation would ensure accommodation for pregnancy-related and menopause-related conditions in the workplace.
Cephas emphasized both bills provide overdue protection and support for menopause, especially regarding the economic challenges that arise. She said many people are not able to access the FDA approved treatments for their symptoms and may not even be aware of the available options.
According to a Society for Women’s Health Research (SWHR) Employee Perspectives and Challenges Concerning the Transition of Menopause (EMPACT Menopause) study, in the workplace, more than 75% of women continue working throughout perimenopause and menopause. However, one in four women have considered not pursuing or did not pursue a leadership opportunity due to these conditions.
“Menopause and perimenopause affect our health, our families, our work and our quality of life, yet too many people still feel unseen and unsupported,” Cephas said. “House Bills 1345 and 2135 are designed to expand access to treatment and prioritize the needs of aging populations in our workforce and healthcare system. I am thrilled that both bills advanced from committee this week and look forward to presenting this legislation on the House Floor. Advancing this legislation helps us to break the stigma, raise awareness and ensure health equity.”
The advancement of these bills coincides with today’s ‘No Time for a Pause’ rally to support this legislative package. Cephas will appear at the rally alongside state Reps. Melissa Shusterman and Liz Hanbidge in the Capitol Rotunda.
House Bills 1345 and 2135 will now move to the full House of Representatives for consideration.

Fiedler, Cephas introduce bill for progressive taxation in PA; would repeal centuries-old “Uniformity Clause” from Constitution
Rep. Morgan B. Cephas
September 29, 2026 | 11:22 AM
HARRISBURG, Sept. 29 –
On Monday, state Reps. Elizabeth Fiedler and Morgan Cephas, both D-Phila., introduced a joint resolution (H.B. 2807), the Progressive Taxation for PA Bill, which proposes repeal of the Uniformity Clause in the Pennsylvania Constitution.
According to the sponsors, Pennsylvania has the
fourth-most regressive
state and local tax system in the country, exacerbating income inequality and putting an undue burden on the working class. A significant reason for this, they said, is the Uniformity Clause in the state constitution, which requires all taxes to be applied uniformly to the same class of subjects.
“Pennsylvania desperately needs revenue to fund our schools, roads, public transit, and more, but the Uniformity Clause is one of the biggest roadblocks to getting the mega-rich and mega-corporations to pay what they owe,” said
Fiedler
. “It just doesn’t make sense that a worker making $7.25/hour pays the same income tax as someone making seven figures, or that a family home in South Philly pays the same property tax as an Amazon warehouse worth $70 million. That’s not fairness – it's elites skating by in a broken system.”
“Philadelphia has one of the highest state and local taxes for working families, and any attempts to change that have been stopped in their tracks by the Uniformity Clause,” said
Cephas
. “This clause implements a regressive flat income tax rate, which puts an unfair burden on working families and hinders economic growth. It is long past time to amend the Pennsylvania Constitution. I am proud to co-sponsor legislation to repeal this outdated and unfair clause, and I call on my colleagues to join me in supporting working families. This legislation is an important step toward true equality in Philadelphia and throughout the Commonwealth.”
The Uniformity Clause prohibits the Commonwealth from adopting progressive tax assessments that increase with income. For example, a tax on businesses couldn’t exempt small businesses that make smaller profits compared to large corporations. That leaves small businesses and working people paying the same percentage of their income in taxes as major corporations and the top 1% of earners.
State Sen. Tim Kearney, D-Delaware, introduced the companion resolution in the Senate.
“The Uniformity Clause locks Pennsylvania into a tax system that simply doesn’t work for working people,” said
Kearney
. “It blocks us from modernizing our Tax Code, from funding essential services, and from building an economy that actually works for everyone -- not just billionaires and corporations. Repealing it is long overdue, and I applaud Rep. Fiedler and Rep. Cephas for fighting for working families and call on my colleagues in both chambers to join us in this fight.”
The Uniformity Clause was established in 1874, before Pennsylvania taxed income and wages. This proposed repeal has been introduced twice before.

Research, funding key to improving cancer treatment, healthcare
Lawmakers meet, tour with officials at Fox Chase Cancer Center
Rep. Morgan B. Cephas
September 21, 2026 | 2:25 PM
PHILADELPHIA, Sept. 21
–
After nearly 125 years devoted to caring for people with cancer, the Fox Chase Cancer Center–Temple Health highlighted how research had been and remains one of its greatest weapons in the fight against cancer. The PA House Majority Policy Committee and House Philadelphia Delegation co-hosted a roundtable and tour at the Philadelphia healthcare and research facility.
"Each one of us have been touched by cancer, be it personally or through family members or colleagues," Philadelphia Delegation Chairwoman Morgan Cephas said. “We all know the transformative care offered at Fox Chase, which is a bright light throughout the state. Unfortunately, we must also talk about what is happening to healthcare at the federal level, including the elimination of research funding, rising costs for patients and the looming rollback of Medicaid dollars."
Research funding cuts at the federal level followed an executive order in January 2025, which resulted in the
end of thousands of grants
— according to
Grant Witness
. The cuts are compounded by the Republican tax-and-spend plan,
H.R. 1
, which will slash $1 trillion from Medicaid.
"Behind every advance in cancer treatment is a scientist asking questions and researchers working toward the next breakthrough," said state Rep. Ryan Bizzarro, who serves as chairman of the Policy Committee and is a childhood cancer survivor. "Fox Chase has built a remarkable record of turning research into treatment, saving countless lives. We have a responsibility to understand that sustaining research is the best option in uncovering the next valuable tool in our fight against cancer."
Earlier this summer,
U.S. News & World Report recognized Fox Chase Cancer Center
as one of the nation's best hospitals in cancer care, including five key areas of high performance (colon cancer surgery; gynecological cancer surgery; leukemia, lymphoma and myeloma treatment; lung cancer surgery; and prostate cancer surgery).
“Wherever I go, I explain I live and represent the people of Fox Chase. People immediately recognize the groundbreaking research that has happened here and the tremendous care that has helped countless patients,” Rep. Sean Dougherty said. “As we heard today, federal cuts could have devastating consequences for care throughout Pennsylvania.”
Founded in 1904 as one of the nation's first cancer hospitals, it has grown into the home for top clinicians and world-class research facilities. Dr. Baruch Blumberg earned the 1976 Nobel Prize for the development of the first FDA-approved vaccine for hepatitis B. Overall, Fox Chase scientists have earned two Nobel Prizes, a Kyoto Prize, and a Lasker Prize, and it ranks at the top in Pennsylvania for bladder and kidney cancer surgeries.
Nearly 90,000 patients visit the Fox Chase outpatient center and 100-bed facility each year.
Information about this hearing and other House Majority Policy Committee hearings can be found at
pahouse.com/policy
. Photos to be used for publication can be found on the day of the hearing at
Facebook.com/PADemPolicy
.

Over 1,200 projects receive funding through gaming revenue

PA Black Maternal Health Caucus chairs reflect on 10 years of the Black maternal health movement
Rep. Morgan B. Cephas
September 15, 2026 | 3:08 PM
HARRISBURG, Sept. 15
–
After attending the Black Maternal Health Conference 2026, the Pennsylvania Black Maternal Health Caucus co-chairs shared updates on maternal health care efforts and the PA MOMNIBUS 2.0 legislative package.
State Reps. Morgan Cephas, D-Phila.; Gina Curry, D-Delaware; and La’Tasha Mayes, D-Allegheny, appeared on a panel at the conference on Friday, September 11. Led by the Black Mamas Matter Alliance, this year’s theme was “Rooted in Justice & Joy: 10 Years of Building the Black Maternal Health Movement.”
The co-chairs shared the progress of PA MOMNIBUS 2.0, a comprehensive legislative package that addresses critical disparities in maternal health care and includes measures that would improve access to essential services and eliminate maternal health deserts. Curry’s bill package, Expanding Midwifery Access & Authority for Healthier Communities, was recently signed into law by Gov. Josh Shapiro.
“It was an honor to speak on the panel and celebrate 10 years of the Black Maternal Health Movement,” said Cephas. “I am so proud of the progress our movement has made and the solutions we’ve helped deliver to families across the Commonwealth.
“However, there is still more work to do. The fact remains that, in Pennsylvania, more than 90% of pregnancy-related deaths are preventable. And Black women continue to face a dramatically higher risk of dying from pregnancy-related causes. As we celebrate progress, we need to continue fighting to ensure more Black mothers survive pregnancy, receive the care they deserve and come home to their families. I remain focused on advancing solutions that make Pennsylvania a safer and healthier place for mothers, babies and families, and on continuing the great relationships with advocates on the ground that have made this work so meaningful and impactful in Pennsylvania and beyond.”
“Last week’s conference highlighted years of advocacy, expertise and lived experience brought forth by people who are deeply connected to the fight against preventable pregnancy-related deaths, and I was proud to sit on this panel with my colleagues, Representatives Cephas and Mayes, to talk about what we’re doing to move the needle in Pennsylvania,” said Curry. “We are keenly aware that not all states have the political atmosphere to advance legislation like ours. But we hope that one day Pennsylvania will be looked to as an example of success for all mothers and babies.
“The PA Black Maternal Health Caucus will continue to advance legislation that improves outcomes for growing Pennsylvania families and to use our voices in venues like this conference to share our knowledge, lessons and experiences.”
“It was powerful to reflect on 10 years of advocacy to advance Black maternal health nationally and to showcase the groundbreaking work of the PA Black Maternal Health Caucus,” said Mayes. “Our work is rooted in a clear vision: to end preventable maternal mortality and ensure every mother and birthing person has access to the resources they need to have a healthy and joyful pregnancy and birth journey.
“PA MOMNIBUS 2.0 builds on the progress we have made while tackling the gaps that still exist in our health care systems -- including maternal health deserts, midwifery modernization and breastfeeding access -- that still leave too many families without the care they need.
“We have proven that when we listen to communities and turn their experiences into policy, we can save lives. We will continue that work until every family in Pennsylvania has the opportunity to thrive.”
The PA Black Maternal Health Caucus was formed in 2023 by co-Chairs Cephas, Curry and Mayes. The caucus is focused on boldly addressing the disturbing trends of Black maternal mortality and morbidity in Pennsylvania through strategic, intersectional legislation and evidence-based policy solutions. Four MOMNIBUS bills have been signed into law since the initiative was launched in 2024.

Cephas honors 250 years of the American experiment at historic PA House session at Congress Hall
Remarks call for continued fight to ensure freedom for all Pennsylvanians
Rep. Morgan B. Cephas
September 10, 2026 | 2:10 PM
PHILADELPHIA, Sept. 10
–
State Rep. Morgan Cephas, D-Philadelphia, spoke in recognition of 250 years of American independence yesterday at the historic PA House session at Congress Hall. In her remarks, Cephas celebrated the Semiquincentennial while emphasizing the ongoing work to ensure freedom, equality and opportunity as realities for every Pennsylvanian.
“We must remember not to treat this anniversary like a celebration of something finished, but be reminded that our founders themselves called it an experiment,” said Cephas. “We know the Constitution was written next door, but here in Congress Hall is where it was put to the test. The Bill of Rights was ratified in this building. The first peaceful transfer of presidential power happened on this floor. This is where the experiment actually ran. And it is no small thing that I am standing here today. Because the founders wrote that all
men
are created equal. And then we spent the next 250 years figuring out who they actually meant.
“There has always been a lag, a gap between when freedom is promised and when it actually reaches people’s lives. That lag runs through our entire history of this country.
“The experiment keeps running. But the lag keeps happening. But so does resistance. Every generation has confronted those lags and refused to accept them as permanent. All of them hold America to its own standard, and now it is our turn.
“Let us celebrate how far we have come, and let us be honest about the work that remains. That is the freedom to access the ballot box, the freedom to access quality healthcare, the freedom to a living wage, the freedom to breathe clean air and drink clean water, the freedom to a quality education, the freedom to give birth in a country that does not treat it as a death sentence. 250 years later, that is the assignment, to ensure the promises of the experiment are kept and expanded.”

State Reps. Shusterman, Hanbidge, and Cephas invite the public to a rally for menopause awareness
Rep. Melissa Shusterman
September 10, 2026 | 11:30 AM
HARRISBURG, Sep. 10 –
State Reps. Melissa Shusterman, D-Chester, Liz Hanbidge, D-Montgomery, and Morgan Cephas, D-Philadelphia, are inviting the public to attend their rally to support the
‘No Time for a Pause’
package of menopause-related legislation.
The rally will take place on Tuesday, September 29 at 1 p.m. in the Main Rotunda of the PA State Capitol building. The event is open to the public and media to attend. State legislators will discuss the impact menopause has on a woman’s health and general work productivity.
“Women spend one-third or more of their life in menopause, and yet there is a severe lack of medical research,” Shusterman said. “Menopause comes with a variety of symptoms, the severity of which can significantly impact daily life and work productivity. It’s time for the government to step up and prioritize women’s health at every stage of their life. The ‘No Time for a Pause’ package of menopause-related legislation is working to deliver better care, education and treatments to the women of PA.”
“Menopause and perimenopause affect our health, our families, our work and our quality of life, yet too many people still feel unseen and unsupported,” Cephas said. “The ‘No Time for a Pause’ package is about bringing this conversation out of the shadows, which marks an important step to address stigma, expand access to treatment and prioritize the needs of aging populations in our healthcare system. I encourage the public to get engaged as we work together to break the stigma, raise awareness and ensure that health equity remains at the center of how we shape policy, deliver care and support our communities.”
“Menopause affects millions of women, yet our healthcare system, workplaces and public policy too often fall short of meeting their needs. Women deserve access to the information, treatment and support necessary to manage its impact,” Hanbidge said. “Menopause can significantly affect a woman’s health, quality of life and ability to work, with consequences that extend to families, employers and our economy. Lost productivity and healthcare expenses related to menopause are estimated to cost $26.6 billion each year. We can and must do better.
“Supporting women means responding to their needs at every stage of life, including perimenopause and menopause. We must pass legislation that improves education, expands access to evidence-based treatments and ensures reasonable workplace accommodations. It is time to break down these barriers, advance these bills and ensure Pennsylvania women have the opportunity to thrive at every stage of life.”
All are invited to attend this rally and call to action.

Cephas, Hanbidge introduce legislation to upgrade Employer Child Care Contribution Tax Credit
Rep. Morgan B. Cephas
August 26, 2026
HARRISBURG, August 26
–
State Reps. Morgan Cephas, D-Phila., and Liz Hanbidge, D-Montgomery, introduced
H.B. 2748
, legislation to help make childcare more affordable for Pennsylvanian families.
The Employer Child Care Contribution Tax Credit was established by Cephas and Hanbidge’s previous legislation,
H.B. 1958
, in 2024. That same year, the national average cost of childcare rose to $13,128 per year, according to a report from
Child Care Aware of America
.
House Bill 2748 provides an incentive for more Pennsylvania businesses to participate in the Employer Child Care Contribution Tax Credit. This bill would increase the tax credit amount that employers can receive from 30% to 100% of their employees’ eligible childcare costs. It also would raise the employer’s annual contribution limit from $500 to $10,000 per employee and increase the maximum tax credit that can be awarded annually to employers from $150 per employee to $10,000. Total tax credits would be capped at $10 million each year.
“Our tax incentive helped working families, but as the cost of childcare continues to rise, we must adjust it,” Cephas said. “This upgraded tax credit will encourage more businesses to participate in this program. By encouraging more employers to provide financial support for employee childcare expenses, this legislation is an important step toward making childcare more affordable for families across the commonwealth.
“Furthermore, working parents who know that their children are in safe and quality care can better concentrate on their day-to-day work and overall careers. This creates a more stable workforce in Pennsylvania while continuing to help families re-enter the job market.”
"Childcare costs are placing an enormous strain on Pennsylvania families, and we need to do more to make quality care affordable and accessible,” Hanbidge said. “By expanding the Employer Child Care Contribution Tax Credit, we can give businesses a stronger incentive to help their employees cover these costs while putting more money back in the pockets of working families. This legislation builds on our previous efforts and is a step toward making childcare more affordable across Pennsylvania.”
House Bill 2748 was referred to the House Finance Committee for consideration.

The PA Black Maternal Health Caucus chairs, Reps. Morgan Cephas, La’Tasha D. Mayes and Gina Curry, have praised the funding allocations embedded in the budget for moms and birthing people in the Commonwealth.
In the 2026-27 state budget, the following investments are being made, totaling $38,586,000:

Cephas announces $2.45 million in RACP grant funding for community
Rep. Morgan B. Cephas
July 17, 2026 | 12:06 PM
HARRISBURG, July 17
–
State Rep. Morgan Cephas, D-Phila., announced $2.45 million in funding from the Redevelopment Assistance Capital Program for three projects in the 192nd Legislative District. The awards are as follows:
$2 million
for the Cobbs Creek Restoration and Community Foundation toward a multi-phase redevelopment project to restore and reimagine the historic site as a hub for community, education and recreation.
$250,000
for Overbrook School for the Blind to enhance dining facilities and transportation. Dining facilities will be equipped with nursing stations and bathroom facilities. Transportation upgrades will include on-campus bus loading zones, staff and visitor parking areas, and a redesigned turnaround. Emergency readiness will also be strengthened with a standalone power and environmental system. Funding will also go toward creating a Maker Space and Work Experience center.
$200,000
for Overbrook Farmacy to construct a new center that will include NatureWorks educational workshops, climate and environmental adaptation, a farmers market, a commercial kitchen, and training on sustainable green infrastructure management.
“I am proud to announce RACP funding for these projects in our district,” Cephas said. “The impact of these grants will be felt in the improvements to education and safety, the reestablishment of community hubs, and the investment in sustainability and fresh food. It is great to see state resources go toward projects that bring our institutions into the present, honor our history and will contribute to improving the lives of our community members.”
The Redevelopment Assistance Capital Program is administered by the Office of the Budget for the design, acquisition and construction of regional economic, cultural, civic, recreational and historical improvement projects.

Cephas applauds budget for affordable housing, education, and more
Rep. Morgan B. Cephas
July 15, 2026
HARRISBURG, July 15
–
State Rep. Morgan Cephas, D-Phila., emphasized her support for the 2026-27 state budget, which invests more than $50 billion in Pennsylvanians without raising taxes.
Gov. Josh Shapiro signed the budget on Sunday, July 12.
“At a time when necessities like food, housing and utilities are becoming harder to afford, I am happy this budget will put money back in Pennsylvanians’ pockets,” Cephas said. “This budget increases affordable housing opportunities, making it easier to find and secure housing, and addresses rising energy costs so families can afford their monthly bills.
“This budget also provides a long-awaited cost-of-living adjustment to give more money to our retired teachers, police officers, firefighters and other public servants.”
Cephas continued: “As chairwoman of the Philadelphia Delegation, I must also acknowledge the positive impact this budget will have on the city. It supports smaller local businesses and invests in making our streets safer.
“The budget includes $157 million for the School District of Philadelphia, up more than $20 million, or 7.6%, from last year. Furthermore, it takes important measures to keep our kids safe from bullying, including a $121 million statewide investment in targeted school safety and mental health grants.
“This is a budget that protects and invests in our communities without raising taxes. That is why I was proud to vote yes. I want to thank Gov. Shapiro and my fellow legislators on both sides of the aisle for delivering solutions to the people of Pennsylvania.”

Cephas applauds Clinton Policy Institute’s Maternal Health State Playbook
Rep. Morgan B. Cephas
October 15, 2026 | 4:31 PM
PHILADELPHIA, Oct. 15 –
State Rep. and PA Black Maternal Health Caucus co-chair Morgan Cephas issued a response to the Clinton Policy Institute’s Maternal Health State Playbook.
The 61-page
playbook
calls on states to lead the effort on improving maternal health outcomes, emphasizes the impact of Momnibus legislative packages, recommends states’ successful policies and models, and identifies opportunities for action.
“In Pennsylvania, we have seen the importance of strengthening maternal health data and accountability so we can better identify gaps in care and develop solutions that save lives, particularly for Black women who are at a disproportionate risk for maternal mortality," said Cephas, D-Phila. "This playbook is a valuable resource for state leaders looking to build on proven approaches and ensure every family has the opportunity to experience a healthy pregnancy and childbirth.”
This May, Cephas was amongst the lawmakers from Virginia and Pennsylvania, two states with Momnibus legislative packages, brought together by CPI. Cephas told
Pluribus News
this meeting introduced her to new funding opportunities. She told the outlet, “As legislators we can issue grants, we can pass legislation, we can move policy, but we want to ensure that funding opportunities and programs that are tackling this issue are sustainable.”
Recommendations in the playbook include expanding Medicaid coverage of maternal health care, such as doula and midwifery coverage and access, as well as modernizing and funding birth centers.
The PA Black Maternal Health Caucus was formed in 2023 by Cephas and state Reps. Gina Curry, D-Delaware, and La’Tasha Mayes, D-Allegheny. The caucus is a bicameral group composed of over 50 legislators focused on boldly addressing the disturbing trends of Black maternal mortality and morbidity in Pennsylvania through strategic, intersectional legislation and policy.

PBMHC applauds Shapiro’s Launch of First Apprenticeship Program to Train Doulas
Rep. Morgan B. Cephas
October 22, 2026 | 9:42 AM
HARRISBURG, Oct. 21 –
Following Gov. Josh Shapiro’s
establishment of the nation’s first doula apprenticeship program
, Pennsylvania Black Maternal Health Caucus co-chairs and state Representatives Morgan Cephas, D-Phila., and Gina Curry, D-Delaware, released a statement to express their gratitude and support. The program will expand Pennsylvania’s maternal health workforce and increase access to doulas.
“For years, research has shown us that doula support leads to improved birth outcomes and reduced complications. Doulas provide continuous support throughout pregnancy and the important first year following, contributing to safer and more positive experiences for families," Cephas said.
"However, this care means nothing for families who cannot access it. We see a vast disparity in care for women who are already statistically at risk for adverse pregnancy outcomes, with Black birthing people at the highest risk of maternal and infant mortality and morbidity compared to other racial and ethnic groups.
“By removing barriers to becoming a doula, this apprenticeship program will expand access to a proven network of support, leading more families to better health outcomes during the birthing journey. I am grateful to Governor Shapiro for establishing this landmark apprenticeship program and continuing to invest in maternal health.”
“This apprenticeship program is poised to significantly improve the birth experience for expecting moms throughout our state,” said Curry. “Doula care means access, advocacy, and allyship that adds the support delivering moms need. When we give women the support they need to stay healthy and strong in pregnancy, we see better birth outcomes. This is huge news for the women of Pennsylvania. In maternal health care deserts, like our rural areas and areas like Delaware County, this will add accessibility and increased resources that are desperately needed.”
The Pennsylvania Statewide Registered Doula Apprenticeship Program was established in a collaboration among the Pennsylvania departments of Human Services, Health, and Labor and Industry, and Patients R Waiting.
This is the Shapiro administration’s latest measure to expand access to doulas. In 2024, the governor signed into law Act 115, legislation sponsored by Cephas which extended Medicaid coverage to doula services.
The Pennsylvania Black Maternal Health Caucus, which recently celebrated its three-year anniversary as a caucus, was formed by Cephas and Curry, and State Rep. La’Tasha Mayes, D-Allegheny. PBMHC is a bicameral group composed of over 50 legislators focused on boldly addressing the disturbing trends of Black maternal mortality and morbidity in Pennsylvania through strategic, intersectional legislation and policy. More information on the Pennsylvania Black Maternal Health Caucus can be found at
